memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and put its king to the sword. (Hazor had been the head of all these kingdoms.) Everyone in it they put to the sword. They totally destroyed them, not sparing anyone that breathed, and he burned Hazor itself - Josh 11:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Hazor was the leading city of the region, the head of all these kingdoms. Of all the towns in the northern campaign, this is the one Joshua burns. We should not rush past the hard reality of these verses. Every living thing in the city was destroyed. This is difficult to read, and it should be.

We meet it honestly rather than softening it. This was not casual violence or ethnic hatred; it was God's specific judgment on a specific people whose wickedness had been building for centuries (Gen 15:16). The Canaanite culture centred on child sacrifice, temple prostitution, and deep cruelty. God had waited patiently for generations, and now, through Israel at this unique moment in redemptive history, His judgment fell. This was a one-time act of judgment in a particular place, never a pattern for God's people to copy. The New Testament is emphatic: our battle is not against flesh and blood (Eph 6:12), and vengeance belongs to God alone (Rom 12:19).

The sober truth here is that God is holy and sin is not a small thing. But that same holiness is our hope, because at the cross the judgment we deserved fell on Christ instead of us (Rom 3:25-26). Hazor shows us the seriousness of sin; Calvary shows us the mercy of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does the holiness of God in this passage unsettle you? Why?
- How does the cross help you hold both God's justice and His mercy?
- Do you take your own sin as seriously as God does?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, I confess that I often treat sin lightly when You do not. Thank You that in Christ, the judgment I deserved fell on Him. Amen.

cross_references.label: Cross References
cross_references.text:
(Gen 15:16; Rom 12:19; Eph 6:12; Rom 3:25-26)

Note: This is a hard passage of divine judgment. If it troubles you, that is not a lack of faith — Scripture means for us to feel the weight of sin and the seriousness of God's holiness, and then to run to the cross where mercy meets justice.
